title: Planning Week synthesis and exec asks (working notes)
content:
Purpose

Quick working synthesis from the Planning Week breakouts (Feb 18–20). This doc is an operational artifact: collect the open asks for exec decision, surface key trade-offs to leadership, and map owners for the follow-up cadence. Not polished — notes + half-formed proposals. Use this as the single source for the exec pre-brief we share Friday.

High-level summary (one sentence):
We need to prioritize three cross-cutting investments (Dedicated capacity economics, rollout automation for private deployments, and an updated host-model routing policy) to keep Q3 throughput/loss-of-service risk low while preserving unit-cost targets — with concrete trade-offs on headcount, budget, and launch timing.

Agenda for Friday exec pre-brief (20–30 min):
- 0–5m: Context and what we decided during Planning Week (Aisha)
- 5–12m: Top 3 asks (each 2m, with 30s decision options)
  - Dedicated capacity – commit vs. phased (Marco)
  - Private rollout automation – scope & resourcing (Lena)
  - Smart routing policy – latency vs. cost guardrails (Devon)
- 12–20m: Risk review & fallback options (SRE + Finance)
- 20–25m: Decision points + immediate next steps (execs)

Draft Top-Level Asks for Execs (need yes/no + priority + owner)

1) Dedicated capacity anchoring (ask = approval of two-tier reserve commit for Q3)
- Short rationale: We have three enterprise customers expected to move from Hosted to Dedicated in q3; current estimate of burst demand would create latency SLO misses if we remain on on-demand only. Predicted cost delta vs. on-demand is offset by committed discounts + SLA uplift for customers.
- Proposal: Approve up to $1.2M commit for 6 months (covers 8 x A100-node-equivalent capacity) AND authorize product to open a 10% buffer for short-term bursts.
- Decision choices for execs: approve full commit / approve smaller 3-month commit / deny (force fallback routing).
- Metrics to track if approved: dedicated utilization, cost per token on Dedicated, customer churn risk.
- Suggested owner: Marco Alvarez (infra lead)

2) Private deployment rollout automation (ask = greenlight 3-person cross-functional rapid team for 8 weeks)
- Short rationale: Private installs still take manual intervention (networking, KMS handoffs) and we are seeing 4–6 week install timelines for enterprise pilots; this blocks revenue and wastes SRE cycles.
- Proposal: Staff a focused squad (1 infra eng, 1 platform eng, 1 solutions eng) for 8 weeks to productize the installer, standardize KMS patterns, and create a reproducible test harness for air-gapped installs. Budget: $180k (contingent on sprint goals).
- Decision choices: approve team now / approve but reduce scope to KMS-only / do not approve (we continue with current cadence).
- Success signals: time-to-first-successful-install down to 7 days, installer runbook with <3 manual steps.
- Suggested owner: Lena Ortiz (private-deployments PM)

3) Smart routing policy update (ask = adopt new latency-first policy for tier-1 routes with controlled rollback)
- Short rationale: Current routing mixes by cost and region; new telemetry shows a 12% probability of latency SLO breach under peak load for top 5 routes. A latency-first policy (with cost caps) reduces customer-impact risk but increases expected per-token spend ~6–8%.
- Proposal: Enable latency-first policy for tier-1 routes for 4-week pilot with automatic fallback to cost-first after threshold triggers. Instrument with per-route budget alerts.
- Decision choices: pilot now / pilot later / don’t pilot.
- Measurement: latency tail (p99), per-token cost, triggered fallbacks.
- Suggested owner: Devon Patel (serving-runtime PM)

Cross-functional asks and dependencies
- Finance: Confirm temporary budget headroom for Dedicated commit and private rollout squad (Finance contact: Priya Rao). Need confirmation by Wed (Feb 26) to meet procurement timelines.
- SRE: Support for pilot routing and fallback automation; identify on-call coverage for the 4-week pilot window. (SRE lead: Jonah Kim)
- Sales/CS: Communicate impact to enterprise customers for Dedicated commit option. We need one AE to lead messaging for each pipeline customer.
- Legal: Review the amended Dedicated contract template for buffer capacity clauses.

Unresolved questions and open items (quick list)
- Exact procurement cadence and lead time for committed GPU capacity — procurement/finance alignment required.
- Risk model for multi-region fallback — need an engineering estimate of cold-start risk when routing across regions.
- Customer communications templating for Dedicated conversion — CS wants a draft before commit.
- Impact on Optimize tooling (recommendations for quantization and batching) if routing shifts to latency-first — possible pipeline to update suggestions.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Approving commit ties cash; mitigation: phase commit with 3-month checkpoint + utilization-based release trigger.
- Risk: Private automation squad diverts core infra time; mitigation: timebox to 8 weeks and require demo + acceptance criteria for completion.
- Risk: Latency-first policy increases costs; mitigation: per-route budget caps + automatic rollback.

Comms plan for the company update (if execs approve)
- Quick all-hands blurb: 2–3 sentences highlighting priority changes (Dedicated commit + private installer squad + pilot routing). Product/Infra leads to record a 3–4 minute FYI clip.
- Email to customers: CS draft and legal sign-off within 5 business days.
- Public blog: Only if we decide to market Dedicated capacity improvements — target PR in Q3 if impact positive.

Decision log (pre-filled choices to speed Friday)
- Dedicated commit: [ ] Full / [ ] 3-month / [ ] Deny
- Installer squad: [ ] Approve / [ ] Approve-reduced / [ ] Deny
- Routing pilot: [ ] Pilot now / [ ] Pilot later / [ ] Don’t pilot

Immediate next steps (owners and deadlines)
- By Wed Feb 26: Finance to confirm headroom (Priya Rao) — owner: Marco
- By Thu Feb 27: CS to prepare customer messaging draft for top 3 impacted accounts — owner: Sarah N.
- By Fri Feb 28: Exec pre-brief and decisions recorded — owner: Aisha
- Week of Mar 3: If approved, kickoff Dedicated commit procurement and installer squad sprint 0.

Notes to self / working fragments
- Consider a 2-step customer offer for Dedicated where we provide a discounted pilot month before full commit to de-risk.
- Can we tie pilot routing costs to a temporary credit for enterprise beta customers to blunt churn? Ask GTM.
- Need a short one-pager (1 page) for exec packet summarizing costs and alternatives (include worst-case spend and break-even).

Appendix (links and quick artifacts)
- Utilization model spreadsheet: (linked artifact) ENG-4523
- Customer pipeline review deck: /decks/growth/q1-corp-pipeline (internal)
- SRE runbook draft for routing fallback: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Routing+Fallback+Runbook

---
End of working notes. Add any changes inline and ping me if you want to move any ask off the Friday queue.
